proves.claim: shardJobs returns exactly one gate's shard rows in order, never a sibling gate's, and its query searches the job_id key instead of scanning every job row.

api.io-gate.shard-jobs-key-range.why: Without this test shardJobs can slide back to a substr scan of every gate-shard row on each pull claim, so claim cost grows with the number of gates.

proves.claim: On a board holding 60000 gate-shard rows over 300 gates, 52 of them done, a walk of settleDoneShardGates has a p95 under 1 s over 50 walks, printed beside the p95 of the old substr query on the same board.

api.io-gate.shard-jobs-scale.why: Without this measurement a slide back to a full scan of the shard rows would only show as a slow pull claim on the live board.

proves.claim: A settleDoneShardGates walk with all 52 done gates takes within 2x of the time of a walk with a tenth of them on the same board, so its cost per claim does not grow with the number of done gates.

api.io-gate.shard-jobs-done-gates.why: Without this measurement the per-gate shard lookup can grow with the board's row count and claim cost grows with every gate that finishes.
